svg.title: shoes: architecture
svg.desc: How the shoes service is assembled at start-up in main.rs, how one request flows through the tower layers, the handler, the service and the repository, how errors become responses, and how this compares with Spring Boot.
svg.text: How the service is assembled at start-up (main.rs) and how one request travels through it.
axum 0.8 · tower-http · SQLx 0.9 · reqwest · tracing · PostgreSQL 18
1 · Start-up: main.rs builds each component in order and moves it into the next one
pool.clone() (main keeps the pool to close it)
There is no container. main() calls the constructors in the order the data requires and moves each value into the next one; the order is the dependency graph.
A value that doesn't exist yet can't be passed on, so a missing dependency is a compile error, not a failure at start-up.
2 · One request: through the tower layers in sequence, into the handler, down to the database, and back as a Response
Each layer wraps everything to its right. A layer can answer early (red); that Response travels back through the layers the request already passed.
one async fn per endpoint, e.g.
the use cases; knows nothing about HTTP or JSON
passes &mut tx to each repo call (one per table)
tx.commit(); an early ? drops tx, which rolls back
3 · Errors are values: each call returns a Result, ? converts with From, and IntoResponse turns the error into a status
5xx: error! logs the whole chain of causes;
the client only reads "the database failed"
4xx: debug!; the message includes the cause
the container scans @Component / @Service and builds the graph at run time
main() calls the constructors in order and moves each value into the next
compile error: the value doesn't exist at that point of main()
one singleton bean, injected by reference
ProductService is cloned per request; a clone copies two Arcs, so every request shares one pool
explicit pool.begin() … tx.commit(); dropping the transaction rolls it back
JpaRepository interface, implemented at run time
private repo module; query! checks the SQL against the schema at compile time
